messages:
maria: deploy-bot tried to apply release/2026.03.21 but hit a provider version pin error — provider.aws is locked to 4.2.0 but the module expects ~>4.3. Can we force-unpin for this change window or do a rollback? quiet window starts in ~10m. logs: https://redwood.internal/logs/run-3492

deploy-bot: terraform apply FAILED: provider version constraint mismatch. Plan aborted. run_id=run-3492. To proceed manually: set TF_VAR_FORCE_UNPIN=true or pin modules back to 4.2.0.

rahul: we should avoid force-unpin in prod unless necessary. Is this from the new networking module? which services are impacted?

maria: impacts vpc peering and okta-sync IAM changes — low TPS but blocks the release cutover. If we don't apply now the rollout will be delayed past the change window.

tim: options: A) force-unpin for this window but stage it in staging first, then prod if green. B) rollback the release to previous commit and re-run the module bump in next window. I'm leaning rollback for safety.

lina: if we override the pin we need to call it out in release notes and create a follow-up to re-pin properly. Product/Compliance need to be aware.

rahul: if we rollback, disable the canary traffic shift so we don't end up half-configured. I'll draft the rollback playbook link in a sec.

ops-bot: scheduled quiet window starts in 8m. Emergency apply overrides require two approvals: infra-lead + release-manager.

maria: I have infra-lead approval. @tim can you be release-manager and approve a force-unpin if staging is green? Otherwise we'll rollback.

tim: I can approve a contingent force-unpin: staging must pass end-to-end in 15m. approving contingent. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: manual override requested by maria. Starting staged apply in staging. run_id=run-3493.

rahul: watch for drift on route tables and IAM bindings during staging. If drift >1 route added or IAM policy changes more than expected, abort.

deploy-bot: staging apply completed — no drift detected. run_id=run-3493 status=success.

maria: ok rolling to prod. will start canary traffic shift in +2m. tagging release with: 'provider override applied during window; revert in next release'.

lina: noted — added the override entry to the release notes draft and opened issue #1582 to re-pin provider after the module bump.

tim: oncall directive: if any latency or error spikes during canary, abort the shift and trigger rollback playbook. rahul will lead rollback.

rahul: ack. rollback commands ready (local notes): `terraform state rm module.vpc.aws_route.foo` then apply previous state. I'll stand by.

deploy-bot: prod apply finished. run_id=run-3494 status=success. canary shift proceeding, full traffic in ~3m.

maria: thanks all — closing the window after verification. quick follow-up item: add automated provider compatibility check to CI to prevent this in future.
